tagline: Through Oakland, with the big trucks sent elsewhere.
intro: From the San Leandro line the MacArthur Freeway runs northwest through Oakland to the Highway 24 junction, keeping near or along the trace of the Hayward Fault south of the Warren Freeway. It went in from 1960 beside the old city streets of US 50, which Oakland had renamed MacArthur Boulevard in 1942, and was finished in May 1966 at the cost of about 160 homes in Trestle Glen.

Oakland already kept heavy trucks off those streets before the freeway came, and the ban came along with it. Trucks over 4.5 tons are still barred through the city, which leaves this the only stretch of Interstate in California outside the National Truck Network.

moments.title: Mills College
moments.text: Founded at Benicia in 1852 as the Young Ladies Seminary and moved to Oakland in 1871, the college counts among its publications a journal of arts and letters called 580 Split.

moments.title: Oakland California Temple
moments.text: Five spires on a hill with views across the Bay Area, dedicated in 1964 and the only temple of its church built without windows, until a renovation finished in 2019 put some in.
